messages.reasoning_content:
The user wants me to perform a retrosynthetic analysis for the given input molecule, considering the reaction type is Functional group interconversion (FGI).

Input: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(CN=[N+]=[N-])cc(-c3ccnc(NC4CCCCC4)c3)n2)CC1

Let me analyze this structure:
1. It has a Boc protecting group: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N...
2. It has a piperazine ring: N1CCN(...)CC1
3. It has an azide group: CN=[N+]=[N-] attached to a phenyl ring
4. It has a pyridine ring with a cyclohexylamino substituent: c3ccnc(NC4CCCCC4)c3

For FGI (Functional Group Interconversion), I need to identify what functional group transformation would lead to this product.

Looking at the references for FGI:
- Reference 1: Input has an azide (N=[N+]=[N-]) and the answer removes it (replaces with nothing? No wait, the input has NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C which is a Boc group, and the answer has N=[N+]=[N-] instead of NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C - so this is converting a carbamate to an azide?)
Wait, let me re-read reference 1:
Q: Context: The reaction type is Functional group interconversion (FGI). Input: C[C@H]1C[C@@H](c2ccncc2NC(=O)c2ccc(F)c(-c3c(F)cccc3F)n2)C[C@@H](NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)[C@H]1N Answer:
A: C[C@H]1C[C@@H](c2ccncc2NC(=O)c2ccc(F)c(-c3c(F)cccc3F)n2)C[C@@H](NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)[C@H]1N=[N+]=[N-]

So the input has a primary amine [C@H]1N and the answer has [C@H]1N=[N+]=[N-]. This is converting an amine to an azide!

Reference 2: Input has C=NO (oxime) and answer has C=O (ketone) + NO (nitric oxide or nitrosyl?). Actually looking more carefully:
Q: Input: CC(C)(C)c1cc(C=NO)c(O)c(-c2ccc(C(F)(F)F)nc2)c1
A: CC(C)(C)c1cc(C=O)c(O)c(-c2ccc(C(F)(F)F)nc2)c1.NO

This is converting an oxime to a ketone, releasing NO.

Reference 3: Input has a lactam with OH on the alpha carbon, answer has the same but with the OH removed (dehydrated)? Let me check:
Q: Input: O=C1C(c2ccc(Br)cc2O)c2ccccc2N1C(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1
A: O=C1N(C(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)C1(O)c1ccc(Br)cc1O

Hmm, these are actually the same molecule just written differently. The answer has the OH on the carbon that was part of the ring in the input. So this might be a ring-opening or tautomerization.

Reference 4: Input has C=O (ketone) and answer has C-OH (alcohol):
Q: Input: ...C(=O)Nc4cccnc4C)...
A: ...COC(O)[C@H]2C1

Wait, let me look more carefully. The input has "COC" and the answer has "COC(O)". So this is reducing a ketone to an alcohol? Or adding water?

Actually, looking at the pattern, for FGI reactions, we're typically converting one functional group to another. The most common transformations I see are:
- Amine to azide (Ref 1)
- Oxime to ketone (Ref 2)

2. It has a piperazine ring: N1CCN(...)CC1
3. It has an azide group: CN=[N+]=[N-] attached to a phenyl ring

- Reference 1: Input has an azide (N=[N+]=[N-]) and the answer removes it (replaces with nothing? No wait, the input has NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C which is a Boc group, and the answer has N=[N+]=[N-] instead of NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C - so this is converting a carbamate to an azide?)
Wait, let me re-read reference 1:
Q: Context: The reaction type is Functional group interconversion (FGI). Input: C[C@H]1C[C@@H](c2ccncc2NC(=O)c2ccc(F)c(-c3c(F)cccc3F)n2)C[C@@H](NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)[C@H]1N Answer:

So the input has a primary amine [C@H]1N and the answer has [C@H]1N=[N+]=[N-]. This is converting an amine to an azide!

Reference 2: Input has C=NO (oxime) and answer has C=O (ketone) + NO (nitric oxide or nitrosyl?). Actually looking more carefully:
Q: Input: CC(C)(C)c1cc(C=NO)c(O)c(-c2ccc(C(F)(F)F)nc2)c1
A: CC(C)(C)c1cc(C=O)c(O)c(-c2ccc(C(F)(F)F)nc2)c1.NO

This is converting an oxime to a ketone, releasing NO.

Reference 3: Input has a lactam with OH on the alpha carbon, answer has the same but with the OH removed (dehydrated)? Let me check:
Q: Input: O=C1C(c2ccc(Br)cc2O)c2ccccc2N1C(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1
A: O=C1N(C(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)C1(O)c1ccc(Br)cc1O

Hmm, these are actually the same molecule just written differently. The answer has the OH on the carbon that was part of the ring in the input. So this might be a ring-opening or tautomerization.

Reference 4: Input has C=O (ketone) and answer has C-OH (alcohol):
Q: Input: ...C(=O)Nc4cccnc4C)...
A: ...COC(O)[C@H]2C1

Wait, let me look more carefully. The input has "COC" and the answer has "COC(O)". So this is reducing a ketone to an alcohol? Or adding water?

Actually, looking at the pattern, for FGI reactions, we're typically converting one functional group to another. The most common transformations I see are:
- Amine to azide (Ref 1)
- Oxime to ketone (Ref 2)
